# Error handling UX: prevention, detection, communication and recovery across a product

Curated by Skill Harbor — @owl-listener's error-handling UX skill: design error experiences that minimize frustration and help users succeed, across the full hierarchy — prevention (inline validation before submission, smart defaults, confirmation dialogs for destructive actions, constraint-based inputs, auto-save), detection (real-time field validation, form-level validation on submit, network error detection, timeout handling, permission and auth checks), communication (clear human language not error codes, explain what happened and why, say what to do next, place messages near the source, use appropriate severity), and recovery (preserve user input, retry for transient failures, alternative paths, auto-retry with backoff, undo for accidental actions). Includes the error message format (what happened / why / what to do), error states by context (forms: inline per-field plus top summary; pages: full-page error with retry/back; network: toast/banner with retry; empty results: helpful empty state; permissions: explain the needed access and how to get it), and best practices (never blame the user, be specific, maintain context, log errors, test error paths as thoroughly as happy paths). Honest caveats: methodology only, no tooling; for validation inside a single form it points to a `form-design` skill that is not bundled here. MIT licensed.
